**OpenPayd connects to Circle network for stablecoin-settled fiat payouts**

*The integration marks another embedded finance provider building settlement infrastructure around stablecoin rails rather than relying solely on traditional correspondent banking.*

OpenPayd is integrating with the Circle Payments Network to offer near-instant global fiat payouts to its business clients, using USDC-settled rails to bypass the delays and costs of conventional cross-border payment routing. The integration allows OpenPayd's clients to receive payouts in local fiat currencies while settlement occurs via Circle's stablecoin infrastructure.

OpenPayd, founded in 2018 by Ozan Ozerk, already provides embedded accounts, FX, domestic and international payments, open banking and stablecoin on- and off-ramps. The Circle integration extends its cross-border payout capabilities rather than introducing an entirely new product line. The company disclosed plans for a Nasdaq listing via a $1.15 billion SPAC deal in June, signalling ambitions well beyond its European embedded finance base.

The move sits within a broader pattern of payment infrastructure firms adopting stablecoin settlement as a practical routing layer for B2B payouts. ClearBank Europe launched digital asset rails with SEPA instant payouts earlier this year, and Mastercard added stablecoin settlement to its merchant network in June. For embedded finance providers competing on speed and cost of cross-border payouts, stablecoin rails are becoming a standard part of the toolkit rather than an experimental add-on.

*Sources: [OpenPayd Live on Circle Payments Network for Instant Fiat Payouts](https://coinlaw.io/openpayd-circle-payments-network-instant-fiat-payouts/) — CoinLaw | [OpenPayd integrates with Circle Payments Network to enable near-instant global fiat ...](https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/currencies/openpayd-integrates-with-circle-payments-network-to-enable-near-instant-global-fiat-payments-to-businesses-1036489235) — Markets*

**Itau receives preliminary US national bank approval from OCC**

*Brazil's largest private bank is establishing a directly chartered US presence, reflecting a wave of non-US banks seeking full national bank status to serve cross-border clients.*

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has granted Itau BBA Nassau Branch, a subsidiary of Itau Unibanco, preliminary approval to establish a US national bank. The approval requires the new entity to hold $507 million in capital, underscoring the scale of the planned operation.

Itau is the largest private bank in Latin America and already operates in the US through branch and representative office structures. A full national bank charter would give it direct access to US payment rails and deposit-taking powers, removing its reliance on correspondent banking arrangements for dollar-denominated activity. The move comes as several large non-US banks – including European institutions – are reassessing how they access the US market amid shifting regulatory signals from the OCC.

For European payments and banking professionals, Itau's charter pursuit is relevant on two fronts. It reflects growing competition from Latin American banks in cross-border corridors that European institutions also serve. And it tests the OCC's appetite for chartering foreign-owned national banks at a time when the agency recently rejected Wise's own US bank charter application, which the company has since refiled.

*Sources: [OCC grants Itaú preliminary nod for US national bank](https://www.fintechfutures.com/regulatory-actions/occ-grants-itau-preliminary-nod-for-us-national-bank) — FinTech Futures*

stories.original:
**Survey finds majority of firms planning open banking and AI fraud investment**

*New data suggests identity automation and open banking connectivity are converging as near-term priorities for payments firms, driven by fraud prevention rather than checkout innovation alone.*

A PYMNTS survey has found that 59% of firms plan to adopt or expand secure bank connectivity or open banking within the next year, with the same proportion planning near-term investment in AI-based fraud detection. The convergence of these two priorities points to open banking data being valued increasingly for its role in identity verification and fraud prevention, not solely as a payment initiation channel.

The findings align with developments in the UK and European markets, where open banking data is being adopted for affordability checks in mortgage lending and gambling regulation, and where regulators including the Financial Conduct Authority have flagged open banking's fraud rates as sitting below wider payment benchmarks. The survey results suggest this pattern extends beyond regulatory mandates into voluntary commercial adoption.

The framing is notable because it positions open banking alongside AI-driven fraud tools as complementary infrastructure rather than competing priorities. For European firms weighing investment in either area, the data supports the case that they are converging into a single identity and risk layer underpinning payment flows.

*Sources: [Identity Automation Moves Up the Payments Agenda](https://www.pymnts.com/authentication/2026/identity-automation-moves-up-the-payments-agenda/) — PYMNTS.com*
